I have farmed rice on this small plot in Kaskazini Pemba since I was a young girl, and I know what my land can give me. The soil is sandy and tired, but I do not have money to buy chemical fertilizer from town, so I will carry goat and cow manure from my homestead to spread on the field before planting. I will sow the same red rice seed my family has kept for generations, and my children and I will do all the hoeing, weeding, and harvesting with our own hands, though I may need to call two neighbors for a day each when it is time to transplant.
